paragraphs.text: Purple buds from wild tea trees in Yunnan, made as [white tea](white:definition): the leaf is only withered and dried, never heated to stop its change and never rolled, so each bud keeps its natural shape and the white down that gives the style its name.

This lot was air dried, which is the [Yunnan way](yunnan-white:making) of finishing white tea, without the low final bake that Fujian white usually gets. It is sold loose, as leaf rather than a pressed cake. White tea from Yunnan is [new to the market](yunnan-white:history), and its trade has grown only in recent years.

brewing.text: Yunnan white is brewed gently, as a white tea is, in a gaiwan or small pot, and it gives many infusions; the leaf holds up well.

notice.text: A honeyed, sweet cup, often richer and fuller than Fujian white, with little bitterness, sometimes fruit like apricot or melon and a hay or herbal note. Yabao is sweet and silky, often with pine or herbal notes.
